clue.text: Be cautious at a creek, swimming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving about freely, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to watch your step when bathing at a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges the eight letters of AT A CREEK.
explanation.definitionFit: To take care is a common phrase for being careful or watchful.

clue.text: A collection of untruths (paper thin)

definitions.meaning: as in the phrase 'a web of lies'

explanation.definitionFit: A pack of lies is called a tissue of lies, and the word also names delicate thin paper.

clue.text: Book taken!

definitions.meaning: the Robert Louis Stevenson adventure novel

explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novel has this title, and the word means abducted, seized by force.

clue.text: Remove mass of ice left in pothole

indicators.note: in places the letter for left within the pothole

parts.note: a pothole is a deep natural cave

explanation.surface: Clearing a lump of ice left in a pothole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L (left) inside CAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: When a glacier sheds an iceberg it is said to calve, so it breaks off a mass of ice.

clue.text: Sergeant, say, in mostly rural moves shows bitterness

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the rearranged letters
moves shows the letters change places
mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A sergeant's country manoeuvres reveal resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims RURAL to RURA; 'moves' rearranges it to RA..UR, and 'in' puts NCO between.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment, so it is a synonym of bitterness.

clue.text: Filled with horror inside, nag has tripped

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled to see a nag stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' points to the letters running through 'nAG HAS Tripped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stunned and appalled is the core sense of the word, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Grassy areas with space where performers rest

parts.note: a green is a grassy common area
room means space

explanation.surface: Lawns and open space where actors relax.
explanation.definitionFit: The backstage lounge where actors wait between scenes has this name.

clue.text: Tree like enclosure

parts.note: as means like
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A tree likened to a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Neodymium discovered in ancient city? Divers can get it

indicators.note: discovered in means the element symbol is found within the city

parts.note: Thebes was an ancient city of Egypt and Greece
Nd is the chemical symbol for neodymium

explanation.surface: An element unearthed in an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered in' puts ND inside THEBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Decompression sickness, which divers risk on surfacing too fast, has this nickname.

clue.text: The part of the head in place of worship

definitions.meaning: the flat area at the side of the forehead
a building for religious devotion, as in Jewish or Hindu worship

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both the side of the skull beside the eye and a sacred building.

clue.text: Some meditation needed to prepare for an issue

indicators.note: some means only part of the word that follows is used

explanation.surface: A bit of meditation before publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' points to the letters inside 'mEDITation'.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to ready text for publication in a magazine number.

clue.text: First two go off in banger to get employment

indicators.note: the opening pair of letters of the word for banger depart

parts.note: banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: Something about a frying sausage being put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First two go off' removes SA from the front of SAUSAGE; banger is British slang for sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the act of putting something to use, so it is a synonym of employment.

clue.text: One captivated by arms law

indicators.note: being held captive by the arms word means sitting within it

parts.note: ordnance means weapons and military supplies
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single person held spellbound by weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivated by' places I (one) inside ORDNANCE, military supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is a decree or regulation issued by an authority, so it is a kind of legal rule.

clue.text: University professional meeting a right furore

parts.note: a pro is short for a professional

explanation.surface: An academic and a professional coming together causes a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a loud public outcry or commotion, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Where the weight could be after considering all factors

explanation.definitionFit: A load can sit on the scales, and the idiom means all things considered.

clue.text: Double weight back in the past?

indicators.note: back says the abbreviation for weight is written in the other direction

parts.note: of old means in former times

explanation.surface: A question of whether weight was doubled in times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns WT into TW, then OF OLD follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something twofold has two parts, so it is double in measure.

clue.text: Terrible ado with Skye involving fellows in old country boundary

indicators.note: involving means the jumbled letters wrap round the fellows
terrible shows the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: FF is the abbreviation for fellows

explanation.surface: A fuss over Skye with men by an ancient frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges ADO SKYE; 'involving' puts FF inside. OFFA'S DYKE is the ancient earthwork along the England-Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa's earthwork marked the old frontier between Mercia and Wales.

clue.text: Two rivers around south showing character

indicators.note: around means the rivers sit round the letter for south

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
the Taff is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Two rivers around the south showing personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts S between FAL and TAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is a famous Shakespeare character.

clue.text: Distinct gold garden tool the book omitted

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: omitted means the letter for book is left out of the tool

parts.note: a dibble is a pointed tool for making holes for seedlings
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: Gold and a gardening implement listed apart from the book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omitted' drops one B (book) from DIBBLE, leaving DIBLE after AU.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that is distinct can be clearly heard, the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Weapon exercises in middle of week

indicators.note: in puts the exercises inside
middle of takes the central letters of the word

parts.note: PE is physical exercise

explanation.surface: Weapon drills midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes EE from WEEK; 'in' puts PE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The epee is a fencing sword.

clue.text: Make for the organic stuff?

parts.note: read as 'make into rich soil matter': the verb for turning plant remains into humus

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to convert into humus, the organic material in soil.

clue.text: Gather TV share is in some difficulty

indicators.note: in difficulty suggests letters in disarray

explanation.surface: TV share in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in some difficulty' rearranges TV SHARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest is to collect a crop.

clue.text: Tamper with sounds like a gong

indicators.note: sounds like says the word is heard, not read

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

explanation.surface: Tampering with a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds like' plays on MEDAL; gong is British slang for a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere.

clue.text: A drop of alcohol of little importance

definitions.meaning: weak, thin beer, a modest drink
trivial matters, as in calling something trivia

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase once meant weak beer and is now an idiom for trivial things.

clue.text: Go crazy with rag producing bad behaviour

indicators.note: crazy means jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Going crazy with a rag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges GO RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble.

clue.text: Sample the heart of impressionism in the gallery

indicators.note: in places the middle letter within the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: the central letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Sampling impressionist works at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' takes S, the middle of IMPRESSIONISM; 'in' puts it inside TATE, a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to try a little of it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Bits of yarn to repeat monotonously

explanation.definitionFit: Thrum means threads and also strumming.

clue.text: Rep introducing the king's colour in heraldry

indicators.note: introducing means the agent word takes in the king letter

parts.note: a rep or representative is an agent
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A salesman showing the monarch's colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts R (rex, king) inside AGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the term names the silver tincture on a coat of arms.

clue.text: Take a risk with light beams being sold

parts.note: to bet is to gamble
rayed means having rays or beams

explanation.surface: Gambling under bright spotlights while being sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold, in the slang sense, is to be double-crossed, the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: A bloomer? Show anxiety and look into it

indicators.note: into means the look word goes inside the worry word

parts.note: to fret is to worry
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Someone makes a blunder, frets, and investigates it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts LO inside FRET. 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is a small flower, something that blooms.

clue.text: Trample on garden endlessly? That's what crowd in a rush do

definitions.text: That's what crowd in a rush do

parts.note: to stamp on is to trample

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the garden

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden

explanation.surface: A crowd rushing across and trampling a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts N from EDEN, leaving EDE after STAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd in a rush surges in a panicked mass, which is the verb's meaning.
